newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Treasury meets Ankara metro debt payments.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Treasury meets Ankara metro debt payments.

text.p: Turkey's Treasury has taken over Ankara's debt repayments on an underground light railway in the capital because the city council was unable to meet its obligations, the city's mayor said on Thursday.

"If the council put in all its money this would not finish in 25 years. There is no other way. Certainly the Treasury will pay," mayor Melih Gokcek was quoted as telling reporters by state-run Anatolian news agency.
Ankara issued Eurobonds and signed agreements for World Bank and syndicated loans to finance its underground railway system, along with sewage and tap water projects costing around $3 billion.
Gokcek, from Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party, asked the government to take over responsibility for the projects shortly after becoming mayor in 1994.
A major portion of the city's debt, primarily long-term, is guaranteed by the Treasury.
